crossStoryFindings: Stories 1-7 are wired end-to-end through shared contracts, Convex tables, Fastify routes, and client archive surfaces, and both requested verification gates succeeded.

The cross-story happy path works, but the execution-to-archive handoff still breaks canonical-truth guarantees in two places: production runs emit placeholder archive content, and deferred entries are dropped instead of downgraded when provenance/checkpoint resolution fails.
architectureFindings: The archive storage/read architecture is coherent, but the execution boundary drifts from the tech design: `createApp` composes a real provider registry while `ScriptExecutionService` still defaults to a canned payload instead of a process-specific runtime.

Turn and derived-view GET reads rebuild projections on every request rather than primarily serving cached projections, which weakens the bounded-read strategy described in the tech design for long histories.
epicCoverageAssessment: Implemented coverage is strong on the green path: archive persistence, archive APIs, turn derivation, derived-view responses, and provenance enrichment all shipped and `corepack pnpm run green-verify` plus `corepack pnpm run verify-all` both succeeded.
Coverage is incomplete on degraded production behavior: there is no protection against losing deferred canonical entries when artifact/source linkage cannot be resolved at append time.
The epic gate passed, but the `test:e2e` leg is still scaffold-only, so no executable browser/runtime end-to-end archive scenario is currently enforced by automation.
productionPathFindings: The in-memory/failing provider adapters and stub checkpoint writer are clearly test-only seams and are not the material concern.

The material non-real production path is `ScriptExecutionService`'s default payload, which fabricates a `Default Execution Summary`, canned reasoning/tool/model/process archive entries, and a dummy source checkpoint note for writable repos.

When deferred archive entries depend on artifact or source provenance, the production orchestrator currently skips the entry entirely if that relation cannot be resolved, creating a missing-history path instead of a degraded-but-readable canonical archive record.

blockingFindings.title: Production executions still archive placeholder output instead of real process work
blockingFindings.evidence: The production composition root instantiates `new ScriptExecutionService(providerAdapterRegistry)` with no custom payload factory (`apps/platform/server/app.ts:285-286`), so runtime execution falls back to `buildDefaultScriptPayload`. That default script writes a `Default Execution Summary`, emits canned `reasoning`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `model_message`, `process_event`, and `script_emission` archive entries, and stages a dummy writable-source file with commit message `Record default execution note` (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/script-execution.service.ts:15-317`).

blockingFindings.title: Deferred archive entries are silently dropped when provenance or checkpoint relations cannot be resolved
blockingFindings.evidence: The orchestrator defers entries with `artifactCheckpointIndex` or `sourceProvenanceBinding`, but `appendDeferredArchiveEntries` uses `continue` when the related artifact version or source provenance record is missing (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/process-environment.service.ts:783-810`). A direct repro against that helper returned `{"entries":[],"page":{"cursor":null,"nextCursor":null,"hasMore":false}}` after attempting to append a deferred `script_emission` entry with unresolved relations, so canonical history is lost instead of surfaced as degraded metadata.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Turn and derived-view reads bypass the intended cache-first bounded-read design
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: Every `GET /archive/turns` request forces `rebuildTurns` before listing turns (`apps/platform/server/services/archive/turn-derivation.service.ts:61-85`), and `GET /archive/derived-views` likewise rebuilds turns and rewrites stored views on read (`apps/platform/server/services/archive/derived-archive-view.service.ts:50-75`). This preserves correctness today but adds avoidable full-archive work and write amplification on normal reads.

unresolvedItems: Decide whether the placeholder execution payload is an explicit temporary stopgap or an unintended leftover from Epic 3; either way it should not ship as canonical archive truth.
No executable e2e suite currently verifies the browser/runtime archive flow because `test:e2e` is scaffold-only.

crossStoryFindings: Canonical archive append/read, turn derivation, derived-view routes, and client surfaces are implemented end to end, and both `green-verify` and `verify-all` passed.

The degraded-state story is inconsistent across surfaces: archive-entry degradation is computed in the archive read service, but turn and derived-view rebuilds read raw archive rows and can report the same process slice as `ready`.

The deferred finalization path is not lossless. Under partial artifact/provenance failure it can drop finalized entries entirely, which breaks reopen consistency and any later turn/view derivation that depends on the archive as canonical truth.
architectureFindings: `ArchiveReadService` bypasses the existing source-provenance read service and rehydrates source provenance from raw store rows, so archive-source coherence can drift from the rest of the source domain.
Flow 7 in the tech design says archive, turns, and derived views use cursor-bounded reads; derived views currently implement only a hard `slice(0, 50)` with no cursor/query contract.
The production runtime still exercises archive finalization through the shared default placeholder script payload rather than process-type-specific execution logic.
epicCoverageAssessment: Happy-path coverage is strong: durable archive tables, archive routes, turn rebuilds, structural derived views, provenance enrichment, and client rendering are all present and exercised by passing tests.

Coverage is weak for degraded reopen scenarios. The existing suites assert missing-record degradation on archive reads, but they do not catch deferred-entry loss, turn/view degradation drift, or source-detach/access-revocation behavior after reopen.
Epic 7 is close on the happy path, but the current implementation does not fully preserve the 'archive stays visible and projections degrade locally' contract under partial-failure conditions.
productionPathFindings: I did not find the in-memory provider fake wired into production; the material non-real path is the real runtime default in `ScriptExecutionService`, which still emits a canned 'default execution payload'.
`appendDeferredArchiveEntries` has a lossy production branch: unresolved artifact/source bindings cause the code to skip the finalized entry instead of persisting a degraded canonical row.

blockingFindings.title: Deferred archive entries are silently dropped when related artifact or source provenance cannot be resolved
blockingFindings.evidence: `appendDeferredArchiveEntries` resolves `artifactCheckpointIndex` / `sourceProvenanceBinding` and then `continue`s when either lookup is missing (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/process-environment.service.ts` lines 783-810). That drops finalized deferred entries instead of appending a degraded archive row, violating the archive-truth requirement when checkpoint/provenance side effects partially fail.

blockingFindings.title: Turn and derived-view rebuilds ignore related-context degradation computed by archive reads
blockingFindings.evidence: `TurnDerivationService.rebuildTurns` pages raw archive rows from `platformStore.listArchiveEntries` (`apps/platform/server/services/archive/turn-derivation.service.ts` lines 48-50 and 89-111) and only degrades turns when the stored row already has `entryStatus === 'degraded'` (lines 149-154). Missing artifact/source context is added later by `ArchiveReadService` (`apps/platform/server/services/archive/archive-read.service.ts` lines 163-224), so turns and derived views can stay `ready` while the archive page shows degraded entries.

blockingFindings.title: Archive reopen bypasses source-provenance degradation logic for detached or revoked sources
blockingFindings.evidence: `ArchiveReadService` loads raw `StoredSourceProvenanceRecord` rows and copies their stored `entryStatus` / `degradationReason` directly into archive responses (`apps/platform/server/services/archive/archive-read.service.ts` lines 120-125 and 198-212). The actual read-time degradation logic for detached/redacted/unavailable sources lives in `DefaultSourceProvenanceService.listProcessSourceProvenance` / `buildSourceProvenanceEntry` (`apps/platform/server/services/sources/source-provenance.service.ts` lines 153-199 and 223-285). A source that later detaches or loses access will still read as `ready` in the archive.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Derived-view reads are bounded but not cursor-paginated as designed
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: Flow 7 says archive entries, turns, and derived views use cursor pagination with default limits (`docs/spec-build/v2/epics/07--archive-and-derived-views/tech-design.md` lines 668-674). The derived-view route schema has no querystring contract (`apps/platform/server/schemas/archive.ts` lines 37-46), and the service simply `slice(0, 50)`s the computed set (`apps/platform/server/services/archive/derived-archive-view.service.ts` lines 210-211).

nonBlockingFindings.title: Production execution still runs through a placeholder default script payload
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: `ScriptExecutionService` builds a canned 'default execution payload' with fixed artifact/tool/archive output text (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/script-execution.service.ts` lines 15-18 and 52-60), placeholder side-work summaries (`lines 233-236`), and an explicit comment that process-type-specific payloads 'come later' (`lines 279-283`). This is a real runtime default, not just test infrastructure.

unresolvedItems: `green-verify` and `verify-all` both passed, but `guard:no-test-changes` currently prints `SKIP`, so the story gate's extra protection is scaffolded rather than enforced.
Whether the placeholder default execution payload is accepted temporary debt outside Epic 7 needs an explicit product/architecture ruling before treating the archive path as production-real.
